source.title: Londonderry Sentinel, 7 June 1967, p. 10 ("County Councils: Londonderry"); Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8 ("Round up of the county councils"); Londonderry Sentinel, 7 June 1967, p. 17 ("Notice of Result of Elections 1967")
source.publisher: Londonderry Sentinel (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: votes as printed (Sentinel, 7 June 1967, p. 10: 'J. V. Brolly (Nat.) 751; F. Donaghy (Nat.) 726; majority 25'; total valid poll 1,477; Belfast Telegraph, 2 June 1967, p. 8: electorate 1,882, total poll 1,490, spoiled 13)

note: Election of county councillors for the County of Londonderry, polled Thursday 1 June 1967 with the rural district elections (Londonderry Sentinel, 31 May 1967, p. 21, advertises the Middle Liberties R.D.C. election 'to-morrow (Thursday), June 1'; the county result was declared on 2 June, Sentinel, 7 June 1967, p. 10). Dungiven was the only contest; the Returning Officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections 1967' (Sentinel, 7 June 1967, p. 17) names the other eighteen members returned unopposed. The Sentinel prints Donaghy as (Nat.); the Belfast Telegraph's round-up calls him (Ind.). The sitting member is marked with the Sentinel's dot ('member of previous Council').
